The test image shows soybean leaves with:
- Multiple discrete dark reddish-brown spots scattered across leaves
- Yellow/pale mottling or mosaic pattern throughout the leaf tissue
- Spots appear circular to irregular with dark centers

Top candidates: Frogeye_leaf_spot, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Septoria_brown_spot, Bacterial_Blight. Let me check references one at a time.
This Cercospora reference (107) looks very similar to the test image - many small reddish-brown spots with yellow mottling. Strong candidate. Let me check a few more classes.

Based on my survey of all 16 reference classes, here is my analysis:

**Test image key features:**
- Discrete dark reddish-brown spots (6-10 per leaf, medium-sized)
- Yellow-green mottling/chlorosis throughout leaf tissue
- Spots appear circular to irregular with darker centers

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Cercospora_107**: Very dense, tiny reddish-brown spots — spots too small and too numerous vs. test image
- **Bacterial_Blight_17**: Dark spots with yellow halos on green leaf — closest match; the test image shows similar discrete dark lesions surrounded by yellow chlorotic tissue
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Smaller spots with gray center, red border — doesn't match the larger reddish-brown spots in test image
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Very tiny spots on heavily yellowed leaves — pattern too different
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Interveinal necrosis pattern — different symptom type
- All other classes (White_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, Soybean_rust, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Anthracnose, Downy_mildew, etc.) are clearly not matching

The combination of discrete dark spots with yellow halos/mottling on an otherwise green leaf best matches **Bacterial_Blight**. The angular-to-irregular dark lesions with surrounding yellow chlorotic tissue seen in Bacterial_Blight_17 most closely resembles the test image pattern.
